question.text: A trader buys a Nifty put with strike 17,000 at premium Rs. 90. Nifty closes at 16,800 at expiry. What is the profit per unit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Put Profit = max(X - S, 0) - Premium. With X = 17,000, S = 16,800, and Premium = Rs. 90, payoff = 17,000 - 16,800 = Rs. 200 and profit = 200 - 90 = Rs. 110 per unit. Spot 16,800 is below the put BEP of 16,910, so the position is profitable. The Trap: Rs. 200 is the payoff before deducting the premium, not the profit. Rs. 90 wrongly returns the premium itself. Rs. 290 adds the premium instead of subtracting it. Note: Broken comparison fragment after "Spot 16,800" repaired — explanation now states explicitly that spot is below the put BEP of 16,910 and the position is profitable.
